# AES Control FSM Behavioral Specification

## 1. Scope

This specification describes the behavior of the AES main control FSM module. The module is the central controller for an AES datapath. It is responsible for:

- Coordinating the loading of initial keys, initialization vectors (IVs), and input data blocks into the cipher datapath.
- Starting and completing encryption or decryption operations in ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR modes.
- Managing manual and automatic operation.
- Handling key sideload selection.
- Controlling pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) data requests and reseed operations.
- Clearing key, IV, input-data, and output-data registers with pseudo-random data.
- Maintaining status information such as idle, stall, input-ready, output-valid, and output-lost.
- Detecting control-path faults and responding with a terminal alert condition.

## 2. Configuration and Start Conditions

### 2.1 Valid Configuration

The module must not start a new cipher operation unless the current configuration is valid.

A configuration is valid only when:

- A real AES block-cipher mode is selected.
- No control-register storage error is present.
- No fatal alert condition is active.

If the selected mode is “none” or a control-register storage error exists, the module must not start a new operation and must not accept a cipher output as a valid result.

### 2.2 Automatic Operation

In automatic operation, the module must start encryption/decryption autonomously when all required inputs are ready.

The required start conditions are:

- The key is ready.
- A complete input data block is available.
- If key sideload is enabled, the sideloaded key is valid.
- For CBC, CFB, and OFB modes, the IV is ready.
- For CTR mode, the IV is ready and the counter indicates it is ready.

The module must define “key ready” as:

- All initial key registers have been written since the last key load or clear, or
- No key register has been written since a previously complete key was loaded.

A partial key update must prevent automatic operation until the key is made complete again.

The module must define “IV ready” in the same way: all IV registers must have been written since the last IV load or clear, or none must have been written since a previously complete IV was loaded. A partial IV update must prevent automatic operation in modes that require an IV.

The module must define “input data ready” as all four input-data registers having been written since the last input load or clear.

### 2.3 Manual Operation

In manual operation, the module must start a cipher operation only when the start trigger is asserted and the configuration is valid.

Manual operation must bypass the automatic readiness checks:

- The key, IV, and input data do not need to be ready.
- The current contents of the key, IV, and input-data registers are used to form the operation.
- The start trigger must remain asserted until the operation actually starts.
- If the first required activity after a key change is decryption-key generation, the same start trigger assertion must remain pending through that generation phase and then start the actual data operation.

### 2.4 Start Trigger Handling

The start trigger must be cleared when:

- An operation starts, unless decryption-key generation is still required first.
- The module is in automatic mode and a start request is written.
- The selected mode is “none”.

In manual mode with a valid configuration, the start trigger must not be cleared merely because the module is not yet ready to start. It must remain pending until the operation can start.

## 3. Register Access and Update Behavior

### 3.1 Control Register

The control register must only be updated while the module is idle and no start, clear, or reseed operation is beginning.

Control-register updates must be ignored while:

- The module is not idle.
- An operation is starting.
- A control-register storage error is present.

A control-register update must clear the key, IV, input-data, and output-data status tracking. This ensures stale readiness information does not persist after reconfiguration.

### 3.2 Initial Key Registers

When key sideload is disabled, software writes to the initial key registers must be accepted only while the module is idle and not starting an operation.

When key sideload is enabled:

- Software writes to the initial key registers must be ignored.
- The initial key registers must instead be loaded from the sideload interface.
- A sideloaded key must only be accepted when the sideload interface indicates the key is valid and after a control-register update has been completed.
- After a sideloaded key has been accepted, subsequent changes on the sideload interface must not be sampled until another control-register update occurs.

A newly loaded initial key that is complete must be recognized as “new” for purposes of decryption-key generation and automatic PRNG reseed triggering.

### 3.3 IV Registers

Software writes to the IV registers must be accepted only while the module is idle and not starting an operation.

In CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR modes, the module must automatically update the IV registers as blocks are processed. The update value and timing depend on the selected mode, as described in Section 5.

### 3.4 Input Data Registers

The input-ready status must indicate whether the module is able to accept a new complete input block.

- After all four input-data registers have been written, the module must deassert input-ready until that block has been consumed.
- After the block is loaded into the cipher datapath, the module must assert input-ready again.
- Clearing the input-data registers with pseudo-random data must also cause input-ready to be asserted.

### 3.5 Output Data Registers

The output-valid status must indicate whether the output-data registers contain a valid result.

- The module must assert output-valid when it writes a new output block into the output-data registers.
- The module must deassert output-valid when all four output-data registers have been read, unless a new output block is written in the same cycle.
- Clearing the output-data registers with pseudo-random data must deassert output-valid.

The module must set output-lost when a new output block is written while the previous output block has not been fully read. Once set, output-lost must remain set until a control-register update occurs or a configured status clear is triggered by a fatal alert.

## 4. Cipher Operation Sequencing

### 4.1 Starting a Normal Block Operation

When a start condition is accepted for a normal data block, the module must:

- Load the current initial key into the cipher datapath.
- Load the IV when required by the selected mode.
- Load the current input-data block into the cipher datapath.
- Capture the previous input-data value when required by the selected mode.
- Signal the cipher datapath to begin encryption or decryption.
- In CTR mode, cause the counter to increment for the next block.
- Consume the input-data block status so a new input block can be accepted.

### 4.2 Decryption-Key Generation

If a newly loaded key is to be used with the inverse cipher, the module must first cause the cipher datapath to derive the decryption start key.

During decryption-key generation:

- The IV and input-data registers must not be consumed.
- No output data must be written.
- No block counter increment must occur for a data block.
- The start trigger must remain pending if the module is in manual mode.

After decryption-key generation completes, the module must return to the idle condition and, if the start trigger is still pending, begin the actual data operation.

### 4.3 Completing a Normal Block Operation

The module must not accept a finished cipher block unless:

- The configuration is still valid.
- No fatal alert is active.
- In automatic mode, any previous output block has been fully read, or there is no previous output block pending.

If these conditions are not met, the module must hold the cipher output and assert stall.

When a cipher block is accepted, the module must:

- Combine the cipher result with the mode-specific feedback value.
- Write the final result into the output-data registers.
- Assert output-valid.
- Update the IV registers as required by the mode.
- Return to the idle condition.

The module must not accept or write an output block if a mux-selector error, sparse-encoding error, or invalid cipher-operation encoding is detected.

## 5. Mode-Specific Data Flow Requirements

The module must select the correct initial-state value, output-combining value, previous-input capture, and IV update behavior for each mode.

### 5.1 ECB Mode

- No IV is required.
- The initial state is the input data block.
- The output is the raw cipher result.
- The IV registers are not updated.

### 5.2 CBC Mode

Encryption:

- The initial state is input data XOR IV.
- The output is the raw cipher result.
- The IV registers are updated with the output ciphertext block.

Decryption:

- The initial state is input data XOR IV.
- The output is the raw decrypted result XOR IV.
- The IV registers are updated with the previous input ciphertext block.
- The input data block must be captured before it is consumed.

### 5.3 CFB Mode

For both encryption and decryption, the cipher datapath encrypts the current IV.

Encryption:

- The initial state is the IV.
- The output is the encrypted IV XOR the input data block.
- The IV registers are updated with the output ciphertext block.
- The input data block must be captured before it is consumed.

Decryption:

- The initial state is the IV.
- The output is the encrypted IV XOR the input data block.
- The IV registers are updated with the previous input ciphertext block.
- The input data block must be captured before it is consumed.

### 5.4 OFB Mode

- The cipher datapath encrypts the current IV.
- The initial state is the IV.
- The output is the encrypted IV XOR the input data block.
- The IV registers are updated with the encrypted IV value, before it is XORed with the input data.
- The input data block must be captured before it is consumed.

### 5.5 CTR Mode

- The cipher datapath encrypts the current IV/counter value.
- The initial state is the IV/counter value.
- The output is the encrypted IV/counter value XOR the input data block.
- The IV/counter value is incremented using the standard big-endian counter increment behavior after each block.
- The input data block must be captured before it is consumed.

## 6. PRNG and Clearing Behavior

### 6.1 PRNG Data Availability

Before completing a normal cipher operation, the module must ensure that fresh pseudo-random data is available from the PRNG. The module must hold output completion until the PRNG acknowledges a data request.

Before performing any clear operation, the module must also request and receive fresh pseudo-random data.

### 6.2 PRNG Reseed Operations

The module must support PRNG reseed requests from software.

A PRNG reseed request must take priority over other idle actions. During a PRNG reseed operation:

- The module must not start cipher operations.
- The module must not accept control-register, key, IV, or input-data writes.
- The module must wait for the PRNG reseed to be acknowledged.
- In a masked implementation, the module must also wait for the cipher datapath to complete its internal masking-PRNG reseed.
- When the reseed is complete, the module must clear the reseed trigger and return to idle.

The module must automatically set the PRNG reseed trigger when a new key has been detected and the key-touch-forces-reseed option is enabled. While this automatic trigger is being asserted, the idle status must be deasserted so software does not attempt to reconfigure the unit before the reseed starts.

### 6.3 Block-Count-Based Masking PRNG Reseed

In a masked implementation, the module must count processed cipher blocks and force a cipher-core masking-PRNG reseed at the configured interval.

The allowed intervals are:

- Every block.
- Every 64 blocks.
- Every 8192 blocks.

The block count must be reinitialized whenever the control register is updated. When the count reaches zero at the start of a block, the module must cause a masking-PRNG reseed to be performed as part of that block start, then restart the count at the configured interval.

### 6.4 Clearing Key, IV, and Input Data

When the key/IV/input-data clear trigger is asserted, the module must:

- Obtain fresh pseudo-random data.
- Clear the initial key registers with pseudo-random data.
- Clear the IV registers with pseudo-random data.
- Clear the input-data registers with pseudo-random data.
- Clear the previous-input-data register with pseudo-random data.
- Cause the cipher datapath to clear its internal key registers and decryption key.
- Clear the clear trigger only after the cipher datapath acknowledges that the key clearing has occurred.

After this operation, the input-data status must be reset so input-ready is asserted again.

### 6.5 Clearing Output Data

When the output-data clear trigger is asserted, the module must:

- Obtain fresh pseudo-random data.
- Cause the cipher datapath to provide pseudo-random data to the output-data registers.
- Clear the output-data clear trigger only after the cipher datapath acknowledges the output clearing has occurred.
- Not write the output-data registers if a mux-selector error, sparse-encoding error, or invalid cipher-operation encoding is detected.

### 6.6 Simultaneous Clear Requests

If both the key/IV/input-data clear trigger and the output-data clear trigger are asserted at the same time, the module must perform both clearing operations. Each trigger must be cleared independently when its associated clearing operation is acknowledged.

## 7. Status Behavior

### 7.1 Idle

The module must assert idle when no cipher operation, clearing operation, PRNG reseed, or start sequence is in progress.

The module must deassert idle while:

- A cipher operation is starting or running.
- A clear operation is starting or running.
- A PRNG reseed operation is starting or running.
- An automatic key-touch-forced reseed trigger is being asserted.

### 7.2 Stall

The module must assert stall when the cipher datapath has a finished result but the module cannot accept it because:

- A previous output block has not been fully read, or
- The configuration is no longer valid, or
- A fatal alert condition is active.

The module must deassert stall once the output result can be accepted.

### 7.3 Input Ready

The module must assert input-ready when no complete input block is pending.

The module must deassert input-ready once all four input-data registers have been written and the block has not yet been consumed.

### 7.4 Output Valid

The module must assert output-valid when a new output block is written.

The module must deassert output-valid when:

- The output block has been fully read, unless a new output block is written in the same cycle.
- The output-data registers are cleared.
- A configured fatal-alert status clear occurs.

### 7.5 Output Lost

The module must assert output-lost when an output block is overwritten before the previous output block has been fully read.

Output-lost must remain asserted until:

- A control-register update occurs, or
- A configured fatal-alert status clear occurs.

## 8. Error and Alert Behavior

### 8.1 Terminal Error on Detected Faults

The module must monitor control-path error indicators, including:

- Mux-selector errors.
- Sparse-encoding errors on important control signals.
- Invalid cipher-operation encodings.
- Life-cycle escalation requests.

If any of these are detected, the module must:

- Enter a terminal error condition.
- Assert the alert output.
- Stop accepting cipher outputs.
- Stop writing output data, status, or trigger values.
- Remain in that condition until reset.

### 8.2 Fatal Alert Input

A fatal alert input must prevent the module from starting any new cipher operation and must prevent the module from accepting a cipher output.

If configured to clear state on fatal alerts, the module must force the status and trigger outputs to their cleared state so that:

- Idle, stall, output-valid, output-lost, and input-ready are deasserted.
- All pending trigger bits are cleared.

If not configured to clear state, the module must still use the fatal alert condition to block new starts and output completion.

## 9. Reset Behavior

On reset, the module must:

- Enter the idle state.
- Clear all internal output-valid state.
- Reset input-data status so input-ready is asserted.
- Reset output-data status so output-valid is deasserted.
- Clear the PRNG reseed-done state.
- Clear block-count and status-tracking state.

After reset, the module must be ready to accept configuration and begin normal operation.
